newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up with cash market gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up with cash market gains.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended at their highest level in almost two months on Wednesday on active buying of blue chips in the Tokyo stock market.

Dealers said sentiment was boosted at the open by Wall Street's gains and a firm finish in Chicago Nikkei futures overnight following news of a management reshuffle at scandal-hit Nomura Securities late on Tuesday.

After hitting an early peak at 18,850, the lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended at 18,730, up 140 points. The last time the futures traded above this level was on February 27, when the lead contract ended at 18,930.
Turnover remained low at 13,300 lots with dealers citing Japan's upcoming Golden Week holidays as a dampening factor.
A trader at a Japanese institution said large-lot buying by a U.S. investment house lifted the market after lunch.
He said the June Nikkei would face a strong barrier near the 19,000 level, but the downside looked supported around 18,550 and more solidly at 18,200.
Comments by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita about Japan's economy improving and the possibility of inflationary pressures had no impact on the Nikkei market, dealers said.
Taiwan stock index futures ended sharply up following heavy gains on the Taipei bourse, where electronics shares rose on expectations of a chip price rebound.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 360.3 against a previous close at 351.2 on 1,277 lots.
